Go here for a cup of coffee, discussions, lectures, concerts or parties with left-wing peers. Or simply ooze or have a barbecue in the nice park in front of the house.

voyage.name: Grøndal Centeret
voyage.content: Grøndalscentret is a huge indoor sports complex, one of the largest in Northern Europe. Go for a good game of squash or bowling, do some swings in the gulf simulator or at the fencing operator, or a work out in the fitness center. And wind down in the cafe after wards. It is quite close to the Youth Hostel and Camping grounds.

voyage.name: Kaleidoskop - K1
voyage.content: Kaleidoskop is stage for modern and experimenting theater performances in the heart of Nørrebro, and has been running for 15 years.

voyage.name: Literaturhaus
voyage.content: Housed in a former church, this is Denmark’s first live venue for literature. Here audiences can experience readings by national and international writers, participate in discussions, or participate in events cent red on music, film and other art forms or on their cross-fertilisation with literature.

voyage.name: Nørrebro Theater
voyage.content: Theatre on Nørrebro, with a focus on being the peoples theater, with down to earth plays, often edging over into Comedy. Mostly spoken, Danish performances, so probably best suited for Scandinavians.

voyage.name: Lygten Station
voyage.content: Cultural house and concert venue in a beautiful old disused station building, right by Nørrebro station. The area outdoors has tables and serves beer in the summer, inside there is a stage. Hosts art exhibitions, concerts (jazz and rock), film screenings etc. according to the program posted on their website.

voyage.name: Ungdomshuset Dortheavej
voyage.content: When authorities decided to clear out Ungdomshuset (Jagtvej 69) on Nørrebro, it ended up in an Orwellian nightmare, with widespread riots that trashed the whole neighborhood. The movement behind the old house, is rebuilding and relocating to Nord-Vest. The house is home for the far left, anarchist, and punk movements of Copenhagen. Hosts concerts, parties, open kitchens, Yoya classes etc. Also has a bar, workshops, e

voyage.name: 66°North
voyage.content: This store run by an Icelandic company, sells high performance adventure clothing, mainly for cold conditions, and has both a men's and a ladies section.

voyage.name: Strand Galleriet
voyage.content: A nice little gallery run by a couple from Western Jutland, hence the rather odd name (The Beach Gallery). Nice attitudes, and friendly staff - lets locals borrow paintings home, and see if it fits with their home.

voyage.name: Antikviteter & Kuriosa
voyage.content: With 45 years in the business, this guy seems to be knowing what he is doing, and his specialty is brass.

voyage.name: Veirhanen
voyage.content: This store has a large catalogue and a well-developed website - with most of the items for sale posted online.

voyage.name: Kim Antons & Co Antique
voyage.content: One of the more exclusive stores, dealing primarily with furniture from the 19th century, and prices mostly going from 5000 kr and up (way up)

voyage.name: ABC Antiques
voyage.content: This is one of the more cozy stores on the street, with wide variety from furniture to decor, and pieces going all the way between 18th century and modern classics time wise.

voyage.name: Bungalow
voyage.content: Bungalow has a large collection of home decor and textiles imported directly from India by the owner, but also sells other textiles in a wide variety of patterns and colors.

voyage.name: Stig P
voyage.content: Fashion store for women, carrying Stig P's own brand, and several other international brands. As a twist, in spirit with the street, this store also sells antique kimono from Japan.

voyage.name: Ingerslev Antiques
voyage.content: A cozy antique store, where the dust in the corners and the general mess, are part of the concept - and you can choose whether to have a chat with the owner, or just breeze the store without feeling obliged to buy anything.

voyage.name: Fünf
voyage.content: Five young designers, each running their own brand, is behind this collective on Elmegade. Mainly women's fashion and accessories, but also a few items for the men around, mainly by designer Tolsing.

voyage.name: Goggle
voyage.content: It was one of the first fashion stores to open on the street, run by a Frenchman and an Aussie, who has built an almost fanatical following. Both for men and women, and from the affordable to the exclusive.

voyage.name: Carhartt
voyage.content: A nice store specialized in the Detroit brand Carhartt (and Burton) producing men's apparel. It blends in nicely with the surrounding stores, which mainly offers Danish fashion.

voyage.name: Hooha
voyage.content: Nice little store, with cool wall paintings, and a friendly staff. Runs their own brand where 10 freelance designers does the prints, but also sells a few other hard-to-get brands.

voyage.name: Elektrocute
voyage.content: As the fantastic store name could hint, this underground shop sells clothing connected to the Electronica scene. But you can also browse the internet at the computer in the back of the store, buy one of the carefully selected compilation CDs, and even get a hair cut.

voyage.name: Ruben & Bobby
voyage.content: A curious mix of second hand stuff like games and action figures, fashion, their own designs - mainly inspired from the 90ties. And to add the confusion you can even get a haircut

voyage.name: Ceramist Inge Vincents
voyage.content: Award winning ceramics

voyage.name: Karamelleriet
voyage.content: Wonderful hand-made caramels.

voyage.name: My Favourite Things
voyage.content: Organic skin care and other favourites.

voyage.name: Æter
voyage.content: Record store and DJ events.

voyage.name: CMYK Kld
voyage.content: Unique and super fine graphics gallery.

voyage.name: MALL
voyage.content: Known and unknown design

voyage.name: Elsgaard
voyage.content: Hand-made shoes.

voyage.name: Kaktus København
voyage.content: Sells cactuses of all sizes, from tiny succulents (from 35kr) to huge things.

voyage.name: Ayuttaya
voyage.price: Mains from 70 kr, menus at 135 kr
voyage.content: No frills Thai food restaurant, serving decent courses in a setting you would expect at this price level, wax table cloth, and tacky Thai decor.

voyage.name: Kates Joint
voyage.content: No, you don't get high here, but it is a cozy and intimate place, and a long time favorite of the locals, for its personality and good size portions of food from every corner of the planet.

voyage.name: Lá Lúa
voyage.content: Cheap Vietnamese restaurant, surprisingly good food considering the location and the price, but the environs are definitely non pretentious.

voyage.name: Quattro Fontane
voyage.price: Cheapest main dish go for 64 kr
voyage.content: Decent Italian cuisine, cooked up by real Italians - which definitely isn't the norm in this price range.

voyage.name: Cafe 22
voyage.content: Nice restaurant and separate cafe at the lakes.

voyage.name: Mama Africa
voyage.content: One of the only sub-Saharan African restaurants in the country, crazy chef in the good way, but bring some African patience with you, as the waits can get rather long

voyage.name: Tribeca NV
voyage.content: This place is in a 1930s factory, and does a fairly good job combining a raw New York style loft - in the spirit of the neighborhood, with an Italian tratoria. And the food is excellent.

voyage.name: Kiin Kiin
voyage.price: 8 dishes tasting menu 1150 DKK, 7 glass accompanying wine menu 950 DKK
voyage.content: Expensive, but takes Thai cuisine to a wholly different level, for which the restaurant was awarded its first Michellin Star in 2007. Book ahead on weekends as the restaurant fills up quickly.

voyage.name: Cafe Tjili Pop
voyage.content: Small cozy cafe that gets up and going Fridays and Saturdays with live music and a lively, rocking crowd. Their live music quality is rather high, but is free entry.

voyage.name: Blågårds Apotek
voyage.content: This place is an institution on Nørrebro, and provides good atmosphere, propped up by candlelight and beer. There is Live music going on Thursday-Saturday

voyage.name: Gilt
voyage.content: A bit far away from anything else, this is a good cocktail bar in unlikely surroundings. For Copenhagen the cocktails here are reasonably priced, and the servings are quite big.

voyage.name: Saxons
voyage.hours: Mon-Tue 11:00-midnight, Wed Thu 11:00-03:00, Fri Sat 11:00-05:00, Sun 11:00-23:00
voyage.content: Laid-back bar, which anonymous and little worn down looks, makes for a surprise when top-notch national and international DJs starts swinging the decks, in a nice mix of Hip Hop, Electronica and Dance music. Except for Wednesdays which are designated Reggae nights.

voyage.name: Barcelona
voyage.content: A large bar with a dancefloor, which also doubles as a restaurant during the day. It is very popular and gets crowded in the weekends - when the DJ starts spinning records around midnight.

voyage.name: Cafeen Funke
voyage.content: The rather odd name, comes from a pun in Danish, translating into something like "Will the cafe work?". It is a cheap place, popular with the alternative crowd, and more of bar than a cafe. Sometimes there are live performances.

voyage.name: Cafe Osbourne
voyage.content: Are you favourite premier league club playing? this is your place then. Unpretentous to the extreme, and a few immigrant regulars who come here for a beer, chat and watching football.

voyage.name: Cafe Sebastopol
voyage.price: Brunch from 78 kr, mains from 128 kr
voyage.content: Huge café, with a large outdoor serving area, that gets very busy during sunshine - also serves decent food, so it is a good place for brunch if the weather is good.

voyage.name: Mexi bar
voyage.content: Tequila anyone? what other place to "get things moving", than probably the only Mexican themed bar in the city, on the corner of Elmegade and the square. It is quite cheap too.

voyage.name: Oak room
voyage.content: If you're up for some cocktails, head north past Rust, and into this place in the basement. It is often really crammed, but take it as a sign that the cocktails here are good. Although there are a few misses on the drinks menu.

voyage.name: Gefährlich
voyage.content: A seemingly odd mix of restaurant, cocktail bar, nightclub, hairdresser and art gallery, but it works surprisingly well. DJ starts spinning records for the crowd on the dance floor around 23:00 Tuesday to Saturday.

voyage.name: Nørrebro Bryghus
voyage.content: This Brewpub is an excellent option for starting the night, with good food, and great beer, produces right in the tanks you are sitting between

voyage.name: Plenum
voyage.content: Play it cool with the fashionable Danish students, from the medical faculty of the university. Outdoor seating on the sidewalk opposite the square, and good cakes!

voyage.name: Temple Bar
voyage.content: A nice down to earth place, with old 2nd hand sofas and lounge chairs on two floors, there is an equally worn out, but workable pool and fuss-ball table upstairs, and the speakers are playing non-mainstream tunes.

voyage.name: Understellet
voyage.content: Fancy a round of pool? this place is a bit worn down, but not only have two (worn out) pool tables and a game of fussball. It is also cheap, with beers going over the desk for

voyage.name: Ølbaren
voyage.content: This is a small place, with one of the city's largest selections of beers. The menu is huge and very explanatory. If you're still lost - the clever staff will be able to sort you out. Crammed on weekends.

voyage.name: Global Copenhagen
voyage.content: Underpinning the ethnicity of the neighborhood this nightclub and concert stage opened its doors in 2007. The stage hosts a variety of music from every corner of the globe, and on select evenings (check their website for details) Club Global takes over with DJs from every corner of the world.

voyage.name: Rust
voyage.price: Cover charge for club: usually 60 kr
voyage.content: Rust is where most people head after 00:00 from the many bars above. It is one of the city's best clubs, but also a music stage for rhythmic music concerts several times per week (check website for program).

voyage.name: Spillestedet Stengade
voyage.content: Located on Stengade this venue hosts concerts during the week and weekend, featuring a wide variety of genres including metal, rock, electronica, dubstep, jazz and hip hop, and hosts RUBA'DUB Sundays - "Copenhagens only weekly reggae bashment and the cities loudest Sunday party, every damn Sunday for the past 10 years." - every Sunday at 22:00

voyage.name: Bellahøj Camping
voyage.content: As cheap as it gets, and as close as it gets to the city center for camping. The camping ground has a small shop, and rents out bikes for 65 kr/day. Only open in summer (July 1st-August 31st).

voyage.name: Bellahøj Youth Hostel
voyage.content: Nice clean hostel, with shared kitchen, TV lounge, laundry facilities and a foosball table available. The outdoor garden area is really nice, with barbecue, a mega size chess game, and benches available. Strict enforcement of no-alcohol policy though.

voyage.name: Sleep In Heaven Hostel
voyage.price: Beds starting from 130 kr in dorms
voyage.content: Right around the corner from Tjili Pop - a local bar. Pretty spartan conditions, except for the common area and toilets which have been renovated, but the only real backpackers style accommodation in town - along with the sidekick Sleep-in Green - with an outdoor beer garden, a pool table, free lockers and free internet. The staff are young and friendly and the place is clean. Alcohol from outside cannot be consumed

voyage.name: Urban Camper
voyage.price: 115 DKK bed in 4-bed tent, 275 DKK private double tent, 420 DKK private 4-bed tent
voyage.content: Indoor "camping" with tents set up in rows indoor. Chill lobby with 24/7 service, sandwiches and beer, fusball tables and pinball machines. Wifi, showers, lockers in tents, breakfast, linnen and towels are all included. Paid bike rental.

voyage.name: Globalhagen Hostel
voyage.price: e.g. Bed in six-bed dorm DKK 120/€15.40

voyage.name: Hotel Nora
voyage.content: Nice location near the lakes and the good shopping and nightlife options in the district. It comes with free wireless internet and breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: The Laundromat Cafe
voyage.content: A combined bar/cafe and coin laundry, where you can wash your rags, drink a coffee or cold beer, and read in one of the numerous books, while you are waiting for you laundry to finish.

voyage.name: Brumleby
voyage.content: Brumleby is a small quarter nestled in a triangle between Trianglen square and the National Stadium. It was built in the 1850s by the Danish Medical Association, as answer to a recent cholera epidemic, as a showcase on how to make healthy but affordable housing for the working class. It has been awarded Europa Nostra award for conservation, and it is a nice place for a brief stroll if you are in the area.

voyage.name: Brumleby Museum
voyage.content: Small museum in the old cooperative shop and library. It is run by volunteers living in Brumleby and they are happy to tell you everything about the museum and Brumleby.

voyage.name: Den Engelske Kirke
voyage.content: King Christian IX's daughter Alexandra, who was became the Queen of England was the driving force behind the erecting of this church, which is home to the English congregation in Denmark. The church was completed in 1887, and was built with some impressive flint stone walls.

voyage.name: Kastellet
voyage.content: A superbly preserved and restored star-shaped citadel. First built in 1626 as St. Anne's Bulwark and completed in 1664, it was the stronghold at the northern end of the East Rampart, which arched through the city and remains in the form of the many parks extending down to Tivoli. The Citadel now houses the Danish Defense Intelligence Service, and is a popular spot for picnics. As well as two small museums with limite

voyage.name: Den lille Havfrue
voyage.content: This little lady is one of the most photographed in the world. Designed by Edvard Eriksen, Her statue was erected in 1913 to commemorate a play of the Little mermaid. The poor lady has lost her head several times, and is often subject to vandalism connected with political statements. Many visitors are often surprised by her modest size (1.25 m (3.3 ft) high). The Little Mermaid is a semi official symbol of Copenhagen

voyage.name: Nyboder Mindestuer
voyage.content: This mini-district was built in the 17th century, and consists of long rows of beautiful 2 story yellow brick buildings. It was built to house sailors from the Navy, as it was useful to have sailors in the fleet living in a confined space, so they could quickly be called to duty. Today the houses are still owned and managed by the Danish Defence, although servicemen from all three branches are allowed to rent a flat.

voyage.name: Trekroner
voyage.price: Admission is free, boat costs 35 kr
voyage.hours: Summer: 10:00-15:00 daily, closed the rest of the year
voyage.content: This 18th-century fort was built to guard the sea approach to Copenhagen's harbor in 1786. It has a special atmosphere, and some gorgeous views over Øresund. There are several well-preserved military buildings and fortifications. A restaurant and a café have been opened in a renovated building. The only access is via Canal Tour's green hop on hop off route (summer only).

voyage.name: Gefion Fountain
voyage.content: A large fountain featuring a large-scale group of oxen pulling a plow, driven by the Norse goddess Gefjon.

voyage.name: Den Frie Udstilling
voyage.content: This art exhibition was established in 1891, as a protest against a censored exhibition sponsored by the royal art board — hence the name. Mainly shows contemporary art. The exhibition is housed in a remarkable, restored building that resembles an ancient Greek temple.

voyage.name: Den Hirschsprungske Samling
voyage.content: This collection was founded by the Copenhagen-born tobacco manufacturer Heinrich Hirschsprung (1836-1908), and moved into the current museum after his death in 1911. The museum hosts an impressive collection of Danish 19th-century art in a beautiful building displaying furniture from the artists homes.

voyage.name: Zoologisk Museum
voyage.price: Joint ticket for both the Zoological Museum and the Geological Museum 95 Kr, students 50 kr
voyage.content: This museum is run by the University of Copenhagen. In the exhibitions, you can experience how the fauna changes as you travel from the North Pole to the South Pole, the Danish fauna since the Ice Age, including a 3 meters tall mammoth and the animals of the great oceans. The latest progress in science is brought to life in some very good temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Enigma
voyage.alt: Museum for Postal, Tele, and Communications
voyage.content: So far only stage one of the new telecommunications museum is implemented. Which means that there is exactly one item on display, an old rusty Enigma machine. But it is free and they have a nice cafe and a museum shop with lots of expensive modern design. So if you are in the area it is worth a visit.

voyage.name: Statens Museum for Kunst (SMK)
voyage.price: Adults 110 kr, under 30 years 85 kr, under 18 years free
voyage.content: Seven hundred years of Western art and cultural history lie under the roof of this striking Italian Renaissance building, which is itself situated in a nice park. Blockbusters include: Titian, Rembrandt, Picasso, Leger, Matisse and Emil Nolde. An array of other icons, paintings and sculptures are also on display.

voyage.name: Østerbro lille Museum
voyage.content: small local history museum run by volunteers at the archives of local history.

voyage.name: Fiskerihavnen
voyage.content: Located on the eastern tip of Nordhavn (North harbour). Because of the traffic on Øresund, commercial fishing is not allowed. But the amateur fishermen at Fiskerihavnen can fish from their small fishing boats. The fishermen have tiny sheds, all different, a bit messy, but colorful. To get there you have to zig-zag past Frihavnen (Freeport, closed to the public), mountains of containers, scrap metal, interesting indus

voyage.name: Fælledparken
voyage.content: Fæleldparken is the big park behind the football stadium, the largest in Copenhagen. There is a lake, big trees and a pavilion with a cafe which hosts concerts during the summer, the outfit Salsa Brava also gives Salsa lessons in the park during the summer. Most of it is covered with grass, much of it marked as football fields. Go there for a game of football or another game, a picnic, or just lie in the grass. At Ma

voyage.name: Kaleidoskop K2
voyage.content: Krudttønden is a cultural venue in Østerbro, with a mix of both concerts and theatrical performances, by both national and internationals acts. Also has a small café, that sometimes hosts various events.

voyage.name: Niels Bohr Institutet
voyage.hours: You should make an appointment in advance.
voyage.content: If you are a physicist or just interested in physics, come to the Institute and see the room of Niels Bohr with photos of the staff of the institute when he was the head of it, a model of the famous thought experiment weighing the clock, the archive, the photos of all the famous people who were developing the quantum theory during the so-called "golden age of physics, when even small people could do big things" and a

voyage.name: Park bio
voyage.content: The only cinema on Østerbro, has an atmospheric lobby with tall plants, caged birds, and a café. Plays many Danish and European movies.

voyage.name: Parken Stadium
voyage.content: Denmark's international soccer games are played at this 35,000-seat stadium. It's also the home ground of FC Copenhagen, who play in Superliga, the top tier. It hosts major concerts, and has a gym, bowling alley and a pool.

voyage.name: Østerbro Svømmehal
voyage.price: 30 kr for just the pool, 60 kr for all facilities
voyage.content: Pool, spa, aroma-bath, steam bath, and baby pool are all hosted in a beautifully restored 1929 building, somewhat resembling a Roman bath, topped with a large glass roof. It was the first public pool in build in the country.

voyage.name: Østre Gasværk
voyage.content: This theatre is located in a remarkable old gas storage container. Mainly hosts musicals but also has plays and comedy on the program.

voyage.name: Svanemølle Strand
voyage.hours: 24/7 but there are lifeguards 10:00-18:00 in the summer
voyage.content: Beach with a 130-m pier

voyage.name: Sandkaj
voyage.content: In the summer buy some cold beers or drinks in the nearby Lidl store and drink them on the wooden deck of Sandkaj, jump in the water when you get too warm in the sun.

voyage.name: Langelinie outlet
voyage.content: is a long shopping arcade, located on a promenade along the harbor, where the gigantic cruise ships dock. Several cafes, outlet stores, and souvenir shops (mainly catering to foreigners and cruise guests) have been beautifully fitted into the old stone bulwark. The ice cream stores at the end of the promenade are immensely popular with the locals during the summer.

voyage.name: Moshi Moshi
voyage.content: This is actually 3 stores that are next to each other, and there is nothing here but the most unerringly stylish, minimal, eco-conscious women's clothing and shoes.

voyage.name: Bahne
voyage.content: Interior decoration and houseware

voyage.name: Rambow
voyage.content: A small design boutique fitted into an old communal bathing institution, sells new and old furniture, kitchenwares, electronics from a host of national and (mostly) international designers and design bureaus.

voyage.name: Crazy Chicken
voyage.content: This small place mainly serves as a take away place, but also has two tables available for a quick bite. Dishes out some excellent sandwiches and has menus with different sorts of chicken - as the name might imply - served with the option of several different Mediterranean inspired salads from a buffet (you get to choose 2) and/or potatoes.

voyage.name: Cafe Sundet
voyage.content: Located on the pier with a great view this place caters to sailors and passersby who just come to breathe in the harbor scene and ocean air. Kitchen is mainly Danish cuisine.

voyage.name: Kafe Kapers
voyage.content: Cozy cafe in a big glass cube on central Østerbro in the middle of the Gunner Nu Hansen square. Dogs are allowed in the pavilion section which is covered and heated in the winter

voyage.name: Café Charlottehaven
voyage.price: The daily specials (M-F) at 125 kr are a good deal. Lunch from 85 kr, Weekend brunch 195 kr
voyage.content: Cafe/restaurant in one of the rare big rooms on Østerbro, for both your pocket, taste buds and your health. In the summer you can eat outside in the huge courtyard. Good selection of beer and wine, or you can try the fresh smoothies and lemonades.

voyage.name: Dag H
voyage.content: This café/restaurant is one of the first to open on Østerbro. The place offer early breakfast, brunch, a large and varied lunch menu. At the evening it transform into a restaurant where you can get a 3-course meal, their special Country Style Dish or try out their famous burger. Also a great place for a well made espresso, cocktail and they have much to offer on their wine menu. Last, many of the dishes you can also

voyage.name: Den Franske Cafe
voyage.content: This café has outdoor tables by the lake under trees and coloured lanterns. The menu is mostly café classics like filled croissants, nachos, chilli con carne, pasta, burgers, but during the summer there is barbecue available until the late hours.

voyage.name: Gourmanderiet
voyage.price: Mains from 120 kr, sandwiches and soups from 60 kr
voyage.content: Originally and in essence this is a high-end organic butchery, but an ever growing popularity with locals have prompted the owners to branch out, and offer a Brunch, Lunch and an evening "Dish of the Day", centred around their high quality meat from organic farms. Thursdays-Saturdays (17.50-midnight) they transform the place into a restaurant labeled Gourmanderiet by Night, and dish out fantastic steaks of every vari

voyage.name: Hos Fischer
voyage.content: Is a good, low key, Italian trattoria style restaurant. The menu varies greatly but if you can get hold of the Risotto, it is a treat. Otherwise go for one of the excellent pasta dishes. The Wine is very reasonably priced (for Copenhagen), and the staff is informal, but still attentive.

voyage.name: Romarin
voyage.content: Good, though not outstanding, food at reasonable prices from the Italian and French kitchens, is made even more tolerable by the fact that you can freely bring your own wine and beer to enjoy with your food. Staff is relaxed in both the best and worst way, readily engaging in a hearty chat, but not terribly efficient.

voyage.name: ØB
voyage.content: Beers and Burgers.

voyage.name: Silo
voyage.content: Elegant food with a spectacular view over Copenhagen and the harbour. Do not miss the upstairs deck (18. floor), you can bring a drink from the cocktail bar up there. Or just visit Silo for a drink and the view

voyage.name: Lupa
voyage.price: 120 kr smallish mains. 400 kr three course menu
voyage.content: Plant based bistro with a wine and cocktail bar.

voyage.name: Brasserie Barner
voyage.content: Informal French food at reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Restaurant Frihavn
voyage.price: 90 kr lunch dishes. Most people can eat two
voyage.content: Traditional lunch in beautiful 1895 former half-timer freeport station building

voyage.name: Madklubben Østerbro
voyage.content: Good food at reasonable prices in iconic 1920'ies building.

voyage.name: Geranium
voyage.price: Set menu for 1048 kr, wines double the price
voyage.content: Reopened in new surroundings by chef Rasmus Kofoed who won the 2011 Bocuse d'Or, and is one of the best chefs in the world. The restaurant got three Michelin stars in 2016. The restaurant is along with Noma at the forefront of the revolution in Nordic cuisine that is current waging on. Danish newspapers and guides all agree; if you want to sample local gourmet, this is a very good place to be seated.

voyage.name: Le Saint Jacques
voyage.content: Very French kitchen — brasserie style with white walls, candlelights, Russian icons and more religious symbols than your average church. With the quirky décor, good wines, and the style of the buildings on the square, it does not take much effort to imagine yourself in Paris when dining here.

voyage.name: Gro Spiseri
voyage.hours: Thu-Mon. There are two sittings: 17:30 and 20:30. Book well in advance.
voyage.content: Guests sit close at the long table in the small greenhouse on rooftop farm, so you will get to know some of the locals. The food is based on Østergros own organic production and matched with natural wines. The staff will be happy to discuss the food, Østergro, rooftop farming, community supported agriculture, etc. There is only one menu, but you can request vegan, vegetarian, etc.

voyage.name: Cafe Bopa
voyage.content: A café during daylight, this place morphs into a crowded bar with DJs spinning records during the weekends. Relaxed atmosphere and great for socializing

voyage.name: Pixie
voyage.content: hands some reasonably priced cocktails (a flat 65 kr) over the counter, Outdoor seating on the small square, and brunch, lunch, tapas and an evening menu if you want to fill up your stomach before indulging. Pixie is the name for a series of well known children's books, and the owners have kept true to the name with pretty neat colorful childish interiors.

voyage.name: Dag H
voyage.content: Located on a small square, colloquially known as the little Triangle, this cafe is popular for its huge outdoor serving area, at the end of the lakes, it is a bit overpriced, but the coffee is top-notch and they have a decent collection of Danish and foreign beers.

voyage.name: Docken
voyage.hours: Sun-Thu 11:00-23:00, Fri Sat 11:00-midnight. Early June to late August
voyage.content: With a huge outdoor area and an artificial beach, it is perfect for chilling on warm days. But they also house a restaurant, and the two large raw industrial storage buildings, houses exhibitions and concerts all summer long.

voyage.name: Tap 10
voyage.content: Small cosy place that has 10 interesting beers on tap and make good cocktails.

voyage.name: Bubbles
voyage.content: Champagne and cocktail bar.

voyage.name: Strandlyst
voyage.content: Old-fashioned brown Danish bar with cheap beers, a digital jukebox, dice-games. But non-smoking.

voyage.name: Rye115 Hotel
voyage.content: This is a small local boutique hotel with a cozy atmosphere serving homemade organic breakfast, feels like a real apartment.

voyage.name: Østerport Hotel
voyage.price: Singles from 675 kr if booked online
voyage.content: really central with most trains in and out of Copenhagen just a minute away, direct trains to the airport, it is close to most of Østerbro's main attractions, and right at the outskirts of downtown.

voyage.name: Stay Seaport
voyage.content: Modern hotel in North Harbour.

voyage.name: Comwell Copenhagen Portside
voyage.content: Modern spacious hotel in the North Harbour area.

voyage.name: Den Blå Planet
voyage.content: Largest aquarium in Northern Europe with 20,000 fish and ocean animals from all over the world.

voyage.name: Kalvebod Fælled
voyage.content: Something of a peculiarity, Kalvebod Fælled covers 2000 hectares (5000 acres) of protected wetlands, beaches, forest, and lakes in southwest Amager, rich in wild-life like birds and deer. Nowhere else in Europe will you find such a large area of wild nature this close to a major city. There are quite a few activities available, like bike rentals, horse riding and lots of stuff for the kids. In the autumn many Copenha

voyage.name: Kastrup Fort
voyage.content: Another of Copenhagen's old fortifications, which has been turned into an attractive park. Other than the outline, moat, walls and a few buildings remaining, there is not much to see here in terms of history. But there are some nice views over the sound and you can venture into the open part of the catacombs and see bullet holes from Nazi executions during WWII. A stroll here is easily combined with a visit to Amager

voyage.name: Kastrupgårdsamlingen
voyage.content: Set in a beautiful old mansion-like country home from the 18th century, this museum displays a large collection of graphics from mainly Danish artists, including a large collection of the somewhat internationally known Cobra artists. There are also a temporary exhibition space.

voyage.name: Kongelunden
voyage.content: If you are staying at a hotel or the camping grounds in Dragør, this small forest is a nice place for a stroll, particularly down Kærlighedsstien, or the path of love in English. A reference to a dancing hall once located down this path, it is long gone, but it is still a romantic place on a nice spring day. If you have kids, the open plains facing the water have grassing sheep the toddlers can chase around.

voyage.name: Amagermuseet
voyage.price: Adult: 65 DKK, During July and the Autumn Holidays: 80 DKK, Children under 18: Free
voyage.content: A historical museum in two old farm houses, detailing the Dutch history of immigration on the island, who were invited to the island by the king to dam and farm the island after the Dutch model. There is also exhibits on historical interiors and textiles.

voyage.name: Dragør Museum
voyage.content: A museum detailing the maritime history of the village, including a collection of paintings by famous local artist C.W. Eckersberg (1783-1853), ship models and various quirky items from around the world, brought home by the local sailors. The museum includes a small art museum, Mølsteds Museum, in the centre of the village, and a fishing vessel used under the famous evacuation of Jews under the German occupation.

voyage.name: Flakfortet
voyage.content: A unique 30-km² artificially created island, completed in 1914 as part of the city's extensive fortifications. Until Dubai and the Japanese went crazy with this type of construction, it was the largest offshore artificial island in the world. The island was sold to a private company in 2001, but since it is a protected area the new owners must ensure public access to the island. This is handled by Spar Shipping's thr

voyage.name: Middelgrundsfortet
voyage.content: Another sea fortress that guarded the approach to Copenhagen. It is owned by the Danish scouts.

voyage.name: Saltholm
voyage.content: If you are an ornithologist, nature lover, or just want some peace, it is harder to get further away from it all and still be this close to the city. Saltholm is a large island off the coast of Amager — and you will be hard pressed to find even a local who has visited, despite the fact that the island is closer to most of Amager than downtown Copenhagen. The island covers some 16 km², and is incredibly flat &md

voyage.name: Amager Strandpark
voyage.content: Probably the largest beach in the near vicinity of Copenhagen, artificially constructed some years back. Includes a large sand island and an inner lagoon. There is usually a good range of activities going on, even outside the bathing season, such as windsurfing, diving, water skiing, sea kayaking and some hugely popular beach volleyball fields. If you're visiting during winter you have a chance to show your inner Vik

voyage.name: Bella Center
voyage.content: Copenhagen's prime exhibition and convention center, with over 123,000 m² of exhibition space. Fairly often there is an exhibition and event of some interest to the general public — check the current schedule on their website..

voyage.name: DR Koncerthuset
voyage.content: Part of the public broadcasters new and problem ridden headquarters in Ørestad, this gem designed by French architect Jean Nouvel is the main reason behind the massive budget overruns of the project — with its final price tag approaching USD 300 million, it is among the most expensive concert halls ever built.

voyage.name: Havnebadet
voyage.content: Enormously popular green area and city beach, with enclosed salt water pools, including some shallow ones for kids, and a 5-m "jumping" tower, shower, grill and toilet facilities, and it is manned with life guards. Excellent spot for hanging out with locals on sunny days, and it is quite a peculiar sensation having a swim smack in the centre of the city.

voyage.name: Mogens Dahl Koncertsal
voyage.content: The country's only privately owned concert hall, featuring some interesting architecture as it has been fitted into some old stables. The programme mainly features classical Chamber music, with artists from all over Europe.

voyage.name: Copenhill
voyage.price: 150 kr/hour for skiing. Access to the rooftop bar is free
voyage.content: Ski slope on top of the huge "Amager Bakke" incineration plant. You can ski, hike, climb, walk up the steps, etc. Or you can just take the elevater up, order a drink at the rooftop bar and enjoy the great view of copenhagen.

voyage.name: Field's
voyage.content: Field's hotly debates with a mall in Gothenburg, Sweden, over which of them is the largest shopping mall in Scandinavia. By Danish standards it is certainly huge: 115,000 m² and with more than 140 retailers. But as it is often the case with malls, it is generic too.

voyage.name: ForvandlingKuglen
voyage.content: A cool store inspired by Middle Eastern bazaars, carrying everything and nothing at the same time. The colorful items for sale change on a constant basis. Local artists and designers often sell their works here; home decór, toys, jewellery and clothing.

voyage.name: Green Square
voyage.content: Scandinavia's largest antiquities warehouse with over 10,000 m² of displays.

voyage.name: Beghuset
voyage.price: Platters from 210 kr, À la carte from 85 kr
voyage.content: Danish and French food in beautiful surroundings in one of the old yellow buildings in historic Dragør. Try the Danish lunch with freshly baked bread and Christiansø herrings.

voyage.name: Dragør Strandhotel
voyage.content: This old place is still going strong despite nearing a good 700 years of age. A bright old yellow building, with a terrace overlooking the small harbour. The food is decent and OK, mainly Danish/French dishes, but come here for the atmosphere, not the food.

voyage.name: Flyvergrillen
voyage.content: This is an oddity and a Copenhagen institution. This old run down diner is located right by the runways of the airport — and has become a hotspot for geeky flight spotters and cult followers alike. The interior is full of airline memorabilia from floor to the attic. Outside there is a hill equipped with binoculars to follow the traffic of the airport, and if that isn't enough, Copenhagen's driving schools run t

voyage.name: Cafe Two 0 Two
voyage.content: Very nice French café with outdoor serving. The café is located at Amagerbrogade near Ingolfs Kaffebar. Good service and delicious café food is offered here. The café also has a very good brunch buffet in the weekends.

voyage.name: Kastrup Strandpark
voyage.content: Fair restaurant at the Kastrup marina, with nice views over the water and decent Danish/French food, though nothing extraordinary.

voyage.name: Strandtutten
voyage.content: While this is mainly an ice cream kiosk serving the guests at the Amager Beach, they are famous for dishing out their mushy and famous Tuttenburgers — if you are a hungry beach lion or kitten, it is highly recommended.

voyage.name: Jasmine rice
voyage.content: South east Asian restaurant with great food. Eat in or take-away.

voyage.name: Det Argentinske Vinhus
voyage.content: Argentinian wine, Belgian beer, port and gin & tonic. And maybe some tapas.

voyage.name: Cafe 5-Øren
voyage.content: Cafe 5-oeren was established in 1991 and has its roots in the nearby free air concert venue, 5-oeren. Local and unsophisticated bar. Both smoking and non-smoking rooms.

voyage.name: Cafe Langebro
voyage.content: Established in 1917 and for long a classical Copenhagen bar, now still a relaxed but more modern bar/cafe. Seating both inside and out. Next to the Harbour Park and Bath, which is crowded on warm summer days.

voyage.name: Jaguar Bodega
voyage.content: Classical Copenhagen bar with dark brown furniture and no daylight. Most customers are middle aged regulars.

voyage.name: Marcel's Bodega
voyage.content: One of the very few places on Amager to serve late night drinkers. A simple place most notable for its late hours. Primarily frequented by younger locals.

voyage.name: Ingolf's Kaffebar
voyage.content: Cafe with food and drink. Good selection of beers, including an exclusive Cuban import. Nice big, green courtyard with colored lamps. Live music now and then.

voyage.name: Copenhagen Camping
voyage.content: Camping grounds on the southern tip of Amager opened in 2008, within walking distance of a beach.

voyage.name: Danhostel Amager
voyage.price: Dorm beds from 130 kr, Singles from 380 kr
voyage.content: A large and modern, if a bit impersonal, hostel with many amenities.

voyage.name: Dragør Badehotel
voyage.content: Charming old beach hotel from the 20th century, renovated, in some beautiful traditional buildings.

voyage.name: Dragør Fort
voyage.content: Unique accommodation in an old fort from 1915. Renovations to turn this into an event and conference centre are ongoing, and the owners have created seven fairly nice and big double rooms in the process — each with television sets and private bathrooms.

voyage.name: House of Colors
voyage.price: 580 kr for one person, 680 kr for two, discount for stays of one week or longer
voyage.content: Not quite your ordinary apartment rentals; in a 19th-century house situated in a quiet neighbourhood. Features 3, nice, colorful (as the name might give away) one bedroom apartments with full kitchen, dining table and a small living room. Also has a lovely little garden with tables and free use of old but serviceable bicycles.

voyage.name: Hotel Amager
voyage.content: Modest two-star hotel, fairly centrally located near the bridge to Christianshavn. Rooms can seem a bit antiquated, but the staff is nice and there is free internet.

voyage.name: Hotel Copenhagen
voyage.content: Although this can seem more like a hostel at times, with shared showers and toilets and rather crammed rooms, it is a good price for Copenhagen and there is no curfew, but a doorcode for the door after 11PM. Good staff. There is one computer for internet access.

voyage.name: Zleep Hotel Airport
voyage.content: Basic two-star no-frills hotel, that gets the job done if you want to sleep near the airport for a single night at a reasonable price. Prices can get as low as 299 kr if you book more than 60 days in advance.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Scandinavia Hotel
voyage.content: 542 rooms, most with a view over Copenhagen. The Dining Room restaurant is on the 25th floor.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Park Globetrotter Copenhagen Airport
voyage.content: Just 2 stations from the airport, also next to a post box (just at the corner of crossing) and opposite to a supermarket. Nice price with breakfast, swimming pool and sauna. Daily free drink in reception (a small amount). Chargeable postcards available in reception.

voyage.name: Clarion Hotel Copenhagen Airport
voyage.content: Five-star hotel next to the airport, with all the facilities you'd expect from a Hilton hotel.

voyage.name: Crowne Plaza Copenhagen Towers
voyage.content: The hotel is a bit far from everything but the surrounding office buildings, but reasonably easy to get to from both the airport and central Copenhagen by means of both trains and the metro. In an 85-metre tower you will find 366 modern if simply-styled rooms with facilities and amenities corresponding in general to the upper-midscale standard, something not easily found in Copenhagen.

voyage.name: AC Hotel Bella Sky Copenhagen
voyage.content: The Bella Sky towers soar over the Bella Centret conference venue, and so do room prices there whenever an event is held. Unlike most AC Hotels, it was not purpose-built as such, and thus features some really unusual and quirky design traits, like wildly placed trapezoid windows.
